Deep Dilemmas - 'Would You Rather' Conversation Cards for Ridiculous Debates & Funny Interactions. 200 Original Ice Breaker Question Cards for Adults, Couples, & College Students - Ages 16+ I've picked up a bunch of these conversation starter games and some are better than others. I would say this one is right down the middle. It's a very straightforward concept - on each card is two choices and you're supposed to pick each one. The problem is that maybe half of them are real dilemmas, while the other half are no brainers. For instance - "would you rather live on a 50th floor penthouse with no elevator or have $2 million in dimes". These are the kinds of questions that might as well not be there because everyone just picks one of the answers and there's no discussion needed, which defeats the point of the game. In some ways I feel like they knew this going in - on the side of the box, it's actually printed that the playtime is up to 60 minutes - with 200 cards, that averages out to 3 cards per minute.

All in all, can't really recommend. You could probably spend an afternoon and come up with better ideas on your own.

Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor [[VIDEOID:c9ed210fcea7bd15ff238268da66c6e5]] I really liked this classic game of Sorry. I hadn't played this game in over 25 years, so this is a fun blast from the past.

The game isn't as silly or as random as I remember it. For a random move your pawn game, there is actually a decent amount of strategy involved.

The rules were a bit confusing, since they used the old 1959 rules. Here's my summary of the rules: You can only move your pawns out of start if you pick a 1, 2, or sometimes a Sorry card. If you get a 1 or a 2, then you only move out to the first circle. You only slide when you get on the first part of the slide. If you can't move, you don't move, and you need an exact count to get into the Home square. Follow the rest of the instructions on the cards.

Pros:
+It's possible to win no matter how far behind a player is
+Great rendition of a classic game
+A lot of fun
+Great for any ages

Cons:
-The rules are a bit confusing. I had to clarify some of the rules on the internet.
-The game starts out very slowly
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

text_fidelity_a: OYEFLY Squishy Toy Soft Exquisite Horror Doll Scented Stress Relief Toy Soft Toy Kawaii Collection Slow Rising Toy Decompression SimulationToys Cure Toy for Kid Gift Toys Well, I'm almost at a loss for words.  I had started my review on this wonderful little squishy toy - or at least I thought it was wonderful.  I was saying how fun it was and how these squishy toys are great for stress relief (which they are), and how it kind of smelled like vanilla or egg nog.  I thought it was such a cute little doll.  And I was going to mention that I still wouldn't let pets play with it since there were some tiny excess pieces at the seams that were coming loose.  And I started looking closer at the seam that extended all the way around the middle of the toy, as I lowered one of the arms to inspect the seam where the head and arm met, that area just started coming apart.  And it only took minimal pressure for it to continue to rip.  So then I looked at the same area where the head and shoulder/arm met on the other side, and the same thing happened. It just started coming apart.  You can see what I mean in the 4th and 5th photos.  This should not happen with any squishy toy, or any other toy for that matter.  I consider this a safety concern and am giving this toy one star for this reason.
text_fidelity_b: OYEFLY Squishy Toy Soft Exquisite Horror Doll Scented Stress Relief Toy Soft Toy Kawaii Collection Slow Rising Toy Decompression SimulationToys Cure Toy for Kid Gift Toys

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder System Stunt Kit Playset This HOT WHEELS TRACK BUILDER SYSTEM STUNT KIT is one of the best "stunt kits" yet, because it can be set up in any of four (4) different gravity-defying configurations. You build a basic "stunt base", then choose the build that suits your numbered experience level: High Jump (1), Criss Cross (2), Long Jump (3), or The Drop (4). If you tire of one of the builds, you can easily take it apart and rebuild it into a different one. (The stunt pictured on the box is the High Jump.)

Because I'm experienced with the Track Builder System, I chose to build the Long Jump. (I passed on The Drop for now, because it requires a tabletop as well as floor space for the setup.) This is a high-performance stunt--you load a car into the rubber-band-powered launcher, hit the launcher release disk hard, and send the car up a ramp, around a loop-de-loop, over a wide gap to a ramp landing, and then down the track to exit the stunt into the rest of your Track Builder layout. You can use the "measuring stick" to measure and lengthen the gap (the distance to the ramp), once you master the launching technique needed to send the car through the entire stunt to a successful completion.

Unfortunately, this stunt kit is also one of the most difficult to build. The Hot Wheels instructions are always a bit confusing--the drawings are three-dimensional, but they lack the dimensional accuracy of LEGO drawings. The parts are shown in the instructions in their actual plastic colors, which helps, but the drawings don't always make it easy to identify the shapes of the parts or to see exactly how they go together. However, the Building Instructions and parts for this kit have a feature I don't remember seeing before: letters (A, B, C, etc.) molded into the parts, so you can match the letters (A to A; B to B: etc.) to connect the parts. This, too, helps with the building stage. (Always remember that if you can't get the car to complete the stunt--no matter how hard you try--you probably made a mistake in the build.)

The parts in the "stunt base" (see my first photo below) click together very tightly, and more or less permanently. I was unable to pry the parts apart, even using workshop tools. As a result, the assembled stunt kit cannot be taken completely apart for flat storage in the original box.

This stunt kit comes with only one Hot Wheels car, and you will need at least one more car to fully play with it. All four configurations have suggestions for using two cars (crashing at track crossings, comparing speeds, etc.). The kit has two (2) extremely powerful 4-speed launchers--I love these! The launchers are the best I've ever seen. (They are already set up when you take them out of the box--don't fool with the rubber bands.) Another new wrinkle in this Stunt Kit is that you can use the retail box itself to add interest and difficulty to your larger Track Builder System layout. There are printed ramps and "fire pits" that can be pushed up and locked together to make a platform with more obstacles for the cars.

This is an excellent choice for any Track Builder System layout, because of its versatility, economical use of floor space, and low price (about $24 on Amazon). The only drawback is that it's harder to build than most Hot Wheels stunts.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder System Stunt Kit Playset

text_fidelity_a:
Pantasy Saint Seiya Building Kit, Sagittarius Aiolos Action Figure Level Building Sets for Adults, Creative Art Collectible Model for Home or Office, Soul of Gold - Saint Cloth Myth EX Building Blocks Pantasy makes amazing building sets, with pieces that usually stay together and super clear instructions. There are some untranslated dialogue boxes here and there, but the diagrams are so clear that I was never confused.

This set of Saint Seiya is something of a mix between a figure and a building set. The base is a traditional building set, and then Saint Seiya is a somewhat poseable figure. The neck, shoulders, knees, ankles, and wings have ball and socket joints for articulation. The elbows have gears that limit movement somewhat. The hips can move forward and backward only. The hands have small ball and socket connectors, but they don’t always hold the positions I set.

I usually really like sets from Pantasy, but this one fell a little short for me in the figure itself. It keeps breaking when I try to put it on the stand, or if I try to pose it too much. This is a set you build and then put on display, somewhere it won’t be bumped. I’ve tried several times to get the feet attached to the base, but end up relying on the clear support on the back of the base, which has a rod to attach to a hole on the figure’s back.

I’ve had the wings fall off, the hands fall off, armor pieces fall off, you name it, it’s fallen off. One of the wings has a loose connection and continually falls off. I have built several sets from Pantasy, none with this problem.

I think the armor is actually fantastic, all metallic gold pieces that match in color. Many of the bigger pieces are wrapped in extra plastic to prevent scratches. The bow and arrow are nestled in foam in a separate box; the packaging is impressive, on par with a UCS set.

There are two face options, and an extra hand if you don’t want to use the bow. There are some great building techniques like SNOT, and as I said, the instructions are very clear. This is an 18+ set, but I think anyone could handle it.
text_fidelity_b: Pantasy Saint Seiya Building Kit, Sagittarius Aiolos Action Figure Level Building Sets for Adults, Creative Art Collectible Model for Home or Office, Soul of Gold - Saint Cloth Myth EX Building Blocks

text_fidelity_a:
UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017) This UBTECH JIMU ROBOT-BUILDERBOTS KIT (Interactive Building Block System (357 Piece)) is so beautifully packaged, you’d almost think it was a smartphone or an Apple product. It comes in a heavy-duty, magnetic-closure box that opens like a book. Inside, the main controller, connectors and fasteners are packed in colorful paper boxes that nest perfectly in the big outer box. Is such a lovely unboxing experience wasted on a kid’s toy?

This kit will make either a “Grabberbot” or a “Digbot”. I say “either”, because the building components are extremely hard to take apart--you are NOT going to want to try a rebuild of either completed robot. Some (but not all) of the components are similar to LEGO Technic elements, but they’re smaller and definitely NOT compatible with LEGO.

In an afternoon (about 4 hours), I built the Grabberbot, which I like a lot. Using the Jimu app (iOS or Android), it’s easy to drive, very responsive, and actually picks things up. Grabberbot has a cool, multicolored LED light (you can program custom colors), and he has a voice cube with a large repertoire of sounds (also programmable).

Grabberbot is controlled with Bluetooth--pairing is easy, once he’s turned on or plugged into a power source. He does NOT have a separate controller, so you must have a tablet or a smartphone to make him work. (I use an iPad Mini.) It’s a good idea to charge the controller cube before you start building--it takes an hour or so. You do NOT want to spend an afternoon building a robot, and then have to wait for the battery to charge before you can play with it!

You can’t build the Grabberbot without a tablet or smartphone--you have to download the app to get the building instructions. (This is a pet peeve of mine; I believe that the instructions for building toys belong in the box.) However, in defense of the download-only instructions, they are presented in 3D! If you’re unsure about a particular step, you can rotate the model 360 degrees and look at it from every angle until you’re sure that you’ve got it right.

Grabberbot is more difficult to build than a motorized LEGO set. There are three reasons for this: (1) the instructions don’t always show the elements recognizably or exactly the way they go together (e.g., the sensor box has fewer connector holes than the one shown in the instructions); (2) the instructions don’t always start at the easiest place for the next step in the assembly; and (3) the components click together so firmly, you need pliers to separate some of them if you make a mistake.

Sadly, the color-changing LED light needs to be programmed if you want it to do more than flash colored lights for a few seconds when Grabberbot is first turned on. I did very little with the programming portion of the app, which requires you to identify which of the four servo motors you want to give instructions to (they are numbered), to choose commands for the motor(s), and to name and record the resulting
action. Programming doesn’t seem to be hard, but it does take some study and practice.

There is a charger with an AC adapter included. The red light on the controller box changes to green when the battery is fully charged. A firmware update starts automatically when you first connect the Grabberbot; it takes only a few minutes.
text_fidelity_b: UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017)

text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height When it comes to making things on our own, my household is a busy place with lots of creativity flowing. When we saw this kit, we could not wait to use it. Finally after waiting due to issues in our house which required a lot of remodeling, we were able to try this out. Let's see how it was..

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
This kit is one of our favorites. Being those who love color, we enjoyed the beautiful colored box. The box has a very detailed booklet on it which outlines every single project in the box and tells how to do the project. The photography is perfect and easy to read and follow. The layout and writing is perfect for using with children- both younger and older. There is not only an assortment of ingredients all carefully labeled and packaged, but there are little boxes and other decorative containers that you put together to give or display your creations in. I love that the bags are also labeled with what project it is good for and the page number in the booklet which is part of the box, so you won't lose it.

HOW DID OUR CREATIONS TURN OUT?
We had such fun with this. We enjoyed making the Bubble Bath Bon Bons most of all, and they really did work nicely in the tub. We have not done ALL of the projects yet, but the Bon Bons are the favorite so far- especially the marble method of mixing the colors. The little boxes that you put together are really cute and perfect to give as gifts. We also had fun with the lip mask.

ANY DRAWBACKS?
You will have to buy some fresh ingredients for this kit. That means that your treatments will be natural and safe for the face as well as fresh. Strawberry, lemon, avocado, banana, milk, honey, coconut milk, fine sugar or colored sugar, yogurt, and olive oil. Be prepared to have those on hand if you want to do the entire kit. We didn't mind though as we use these things in our home anyway, except for sugar, but I did have some on hand from a sugar scrub we experimented with in the past.

THE BOTTOM LINE
With all of the more unusual ingredients supplied, this kit is great fun to do. My daughter and I had a wonderful time with it. The colors, layout, and packaging are top notch. With the exception of having to provide quite a few fresh ingredients, this is easy and convenient but great fun when you finally do get to have your SPA day!

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! This can be used from young kids who are able to do this with supervision up to older kids- even late teens- who really want to have fun creating a spa day. I can also see using the principles used in this in the future creating a spa day for grandma or others that the kids want to reach out to for a special day.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height

I personally think that, since this toy set is made of plastic, it is quite overpriced and not a good value. It is priced as if it were made of wood. Further, I wonder why on earth a company that is famed for its high-quality, wooden toys would opt to convert to plastic toys? It makes no sense.

However, if you are not looking for wooden toys for your child or grandchild, the fact that this is just another plastic toy set, in a world already over-filled with plastic, the plastic construction may not bother you. This toy set, on the positive side, does have very attractive, bright colors, and it does inspire creative play, as the older, wooden sets did. It's just not wood!

This set is for children age 3 and up because of small parts and a choking hazard.

text_fidelity_a: Marvel Captain America Disc Launching Shield When I saw this product was available, I thought that I would order it for my 10 year old son, who wants to see the movie Captain America when it is released later this summer. After receiving it, I asked him to write a review from the perspective of a 10-year-old. This is what he had to say: "The Captain America Shield is really fun. It is easy to put together(he literally read the directions and assembled the parts all by himself). I just had to add 4 batteries and place the foam discs in it. When you shoot the discs you hear a sound, like a siren. But the sound can get kind of annoying. Other than that, the shield is pretty fun". From a parents perspective, I thought that (1) the easy to read instructions allows kids to problem solve and work independently. (2) The sound when the discs are fired acts as a warning system (kind of a fail safe although I don't think the foam discs could cause any damage). And if a child ever accidentally fired the discs in the direction of another child's eyes, although I don't think that they will be injured, they will at least hear it coming. (3) The armband and handgrip are perfect for holding the shield. And (4) it seems like fun. While my 10 year old (it was his birthday today) had fun, I do think that a slightly younger child (7 or 8) would have more fun and not become bored as quickly as an older one.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Captain America Disc Launching Shield

text_fidelity_a:
Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure (Due to the malfunctions on our particular dog, and the fact that he doesn't walk at all, I was tempted to give it 3 stars, but he's so cute and fun, I went with 4.)

I have a few Paw Patrol fans in my house, so this is a pretty amazing toy.

By pressing the badge on the front of Chase, your children are given a mission. Chase talks and interacts through these missions. For example, chickens have gotten loose, and your child needs to help gather them up. The net compartment opens up, and your child will fire the net out. Chase comments on catching one, and then asks for the net to be reloaded. (One time the net got stuck, and didn't fire out, but he still exclaimed praise at catching a chicken, so it's not perfect.) He won't interact to various things that your child says, but he does have built in interaction, which is still pretty cool.

There are 24 different missions, and Chase moves around a bit through these. I was expecting him to walk a bit, but he never did. He just moves his head around, and moves from crouching to standing positions. There are two compartments on his backpack. One has a net launcher. The other has a microphone(that your child can talk into) and a flashlight. There are various buttons for each feature. (One for opening each compartment, one on the net launcher to launch, one to make the light come on the flashlight, and one to turn on the microphone.) Some of the items come on automatically through missions, but others require your child's assistance, when Chase asks.

Although this is an awesome toy that I'm pretty sure any Paw Patrol fan will love, we did have a couple of negatives with ours.

When the box was first opened, the head was detached a bit, but thankfully, it went back on pretty easily. Also, the button to launch the microphone/flashlight wouldn't work. I tried everything I could to make it work, short of tearing it apart, and tried numerous times, but it never worked. It didn't work when it was supposed to automatically open during missions, either. Thankfully, we can just pull that compartment open. During missions when a child is asked to launch the microphone/flashlight, pulling open the door makes the task recognized, just as if the button worked. So, it's not a huge deal, but still disappointing.

I really do wish he walked a bit, too! The way he's designed, it looked as if he would.

A couple of notes:
-This toy DOES come with batteries, but require 4 AA if you'd like to buy extras.
-If your child can read, know that the box this is delivered in says what's inside, though there are no pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure

Bobby Fischer® Learn to Play Chess Set Board Game, Easy to Understand - How to Play Chess Book, 34 Plastic Staunton Chess Pieces, Folding Illustrated Chess Board, Family Games for Kids and Adults When I was in middle school, a teacher I did not really know invited me in to learn chess. It changed my life. I wanted to pass the information on to my kids, but it was hard to get them to make connections. This set is great.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
This set comes with a four fold board, big sized pieces, general instructions, and two dice.

BOARD
The board has information right on it, so that you don't have to repeat it over and over for visual learners.

PIECES
The pieces in this box are plenty big enough, have a nice felt bottom and are all in the box. Nothing was missing. There were even the two extra queens in the box too.

IS IT EASY TO TEACH WITH?
I found that this is really easy to teach with and in my case, it has been a while since I could play chess with someone and not a computer, so I found this very exciting.

DICE
The dice is a great way to even out playing with a beginner which helps a lot because who wants to be beaten constantly?

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great set for a beginner chess learner. The board is small, the pieces easy to use and the directions clear and well laid out. The dice make it fun for mis matched players (beginner vs more advanced).

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this set and am glad to have it. My family is finally going to learn chess without me having to continually explain everything. The visuals are great.

Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures Doll & Accessories, Travel Set with Daisy Doll, Kitten, Working Suitcase & 9 Pieces (Amazon Exclusive) The Barbies in my day were just ridiculously shaped, so much so that even in the third grade I rejected them as a model that I would never live up to in my own feminine figure. I remember wishing that I could play with Barbies, but the body shapes made me feel unhappy and inadequate – you might think girls aren't aware of this kind of thing at a young age, but I certainly was. I owned one or two, but they were never something I love for this reason.

So just imagine my delight to realize that Barbie has created so many interesting and diverse dolls now to play with. This Daisy figure has really just a normal kind of shape that you would see on many, many ladies and moms at the grocery store. She looked beautiful, and also has a much more realistic form. I love the styling of her outfit, and her gorgeous pink hair just straight up makes me happy to look at and brush.

The way that they chose to craft Barbies slightly bigger thighs was interesting to me, so I took a photo of it. Overall, this feels like a really body positive, average pretty Barbie to play with, who is stylish and fun and attractive yet doesn't set up my daughter with completely ridiculous ideas of what women might look like.

Even the normal Barbies, I have a chicken farmer Barbie, and a Barbie who runs a doggy daycare, seem like their proportions have evolved somewhat, and then the fact that they are doing normal things like cleaning up dog messes and collecting eggs really goes so far in my book. I also love the Ken doll who is doing his own laundry in his very own washing machine. My husband is a little flummoxed by my absolute flat out glee at seeing such a thing, but I think setting the expectation that Ken will enjoy doing his own self-care chores is an excellent one for young ladies.

Overall, from having the impression that I would never let my children play with Barbies, I've come a long way, and that's because Barbie has come a long way to. I'm delighted with Daisy, and her cool accessories and great look.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures Doll & Accessories, Travel Set with Daisy Doll, Kitten, Working Suitcase & 9 Pieces (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show is a fun way for your little fashion diva to spend some free time. All you do is download the application on your smartphone, tablet, or iPod touch, draw some fashion designs, and then scan them. Your fashion will then show up on an actual fashion model, in 3D, to your child’s delight.

My girls are fashion designers in the making so I knew they would love playing with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show. It takes little effort to get going. You just add the application to your smartphone or tablet, and then have your child start drawing. Once scanned through the application, kids will be able to see their own fashion design on an actual model. This caused squeals of satisfaction from my girls who loved seeing their fashion on screen.

From my children’s perspectives, there is little that isn’t perfect with a toy like this, but as an adult, I can see a few issues. One has already been stated by others who have used the device, but bears repeating: The phone or tablet you use will make a difference. Not all smartphones or tablets are created equally and the colors may look a little off. If you have more than one device and it doesn’t look good on one, then you might want to consider downloading the application to another device. It could make a difference and it’s simple enough to do.

The included accessories with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show are a little limited. The small colored pencils are also somewhat of an obstacle, as they are not good for larger hands. But overall, this is a fun fashion design kit and I cannot imagine a fashion- loving child who wouldn’t fall in love with it.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.
text_fidelity_b: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath

As a die hard Star Wars Fan this Saber has a lot going for it, but a few cons. First the build and look are nice. The sound is also very good. The price is one of the best reasons for getting one. As of today a 40% off coupon making it around $72.00. To me at this price point shows you how much Disney and Star Wars The Black Series is ripping people off.

For the $72.00 you're getting 12 Light Sabers "colors" compare that to $250.00 and higher for one color. Now for the cons the blade is held in place by three set screws and it still has a bit of a lose feeling not much but its there. The other thing is the control button it is a bit cumbersome and by that I mean the holding down or pushing or doing the fast twist while holding button down to change sound fonts. I know some other saber makers use similar features but not this hard to change. One of the sound fonts is not even from Star Wars. I did not know what it was and could not stand it, but you might like. The problem was it took me several tries to change it and it should not be that hard to change.

So even with those two minor faults, this is still a great Saber for the price. As someone who was 10 years old when Star Wars came out, even now holding this and turning it on makes me smile.

"May the Force be with You"

Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit I’m a big fan of the Thames & Kosmos building kits--especially the ones that teach STEM principles. However, this THAMES & KOSMOS PEPPER MINT IN THE FANTASTIC UNDERWATER SCIENCE VOYAGE EXPERIMENT KIT is definitely NOT one of my favorites. The experiments do teach about the physical properties of water (e.g., siphoning, hydraulics), but they are boring--mostly they require operating a syringe to push water through tubing.

The boat is easy to build. The parts are stamped onto thin sheets of wood. You punch the parts out of the sheets, and the edges come out smooth and clean. The parts then lock together without requiring glue or other fasteners. The assembly instructions are included in a booklet that contains a silly adventure/discovery story that features the girl character Pepper Mint.

The story is interrupted from time to time with instructions for science experiments. Each experiment has a good, easy-to-understand explanation of “what’s happening” (e.g., water can move things because, unlike air, it cannot be compressed).

The kit is apparently aimed at 11-year-old girls (Pepper Mint’s age), but the story and the experiments seem rather simplistic for that age group. I do wish that Thames & Kosmos had chosen a more serious name than “Pepper Mint” for their girl scientist. This kit has some teaching value, but it trivializes science for girls.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Prime Climb Great game for helping kids understand factors and learn their multiplication/division (and addition/subtraction) facts, plus it's FUN! The part that initially drew me in for where my kids are was the color coding of the basic primes, and by extension the use of those colors to represent factors in the products. Then, it arrived and the gameplay was really fun--there are two ten sided dice and you can add, subtract, multiply or divide the number you are on by each die in turn to move. If you land on a prime you get to draw a Prime Card, which you can either use right away or save for later to benefit yourself or target an opponent, depending on whether the card is an Action card or Keeper. The first person to move both pawns to 101 wins. If you get tired of the standard rules, though, they apparently have some variations here: [...] but I have not yet tried any--looking forward to doing so after we've played through a few more times.

Oh and keep in mind that it takes longer the more players there are--folks with younger kids might want to keep it to 2 or 3 players so it doesn't go so long, or modify the rules so people don't get sent back to start so often. I'm sure there are cooperative ways to play too if that's more up someone's alley, like it was for us when the kids were younger.

The set includes yellow and pink parts, so you can pick what color the orchid flowers are, and even change the colors if you want.

The set has numbered bags: three #1 bags for the pot, two #2 bags for the flower stems, and one #3 bag for the flower pieces. The instructions say “the numbered bags have no bearing on order of build” but that’s not actually true, as you do use the bags in order.

The pot is nice, it has pearly gold and slate blue pieces. It’s solid, easily supporting the big orchid plant. The plant itself is sturdy, the stems are connected together for extra reinforcement. The pieces stay together reasonably well. There are some loose parts, but not very many for an off-brand set.

The instructions are mostly clear. Some of the colors are hard to see, like the dark green pieces used for the plant stems. For the most part, the instructions point out confusing bits, one step even has an overhead view so you can make sure the pieces are in the right spot. But the very last step has me stumped: adding brown pieces to the pot to mimic dirt. I *think* the pieces just sit in the pot and aren’t snapped to any others, but if so, I don’t like that.

Overall, this is a fun set to build and the finished plant is a nice display piece.

First of all - this is big! Look carefully at the specs on this toy to see if it will fit well (or dominate) your play space. The colors and designs are bright and cheerful, which I like. There are a few specific mechanical steps to make this work right with the car, and I worried that it would be too complicated for my 2yo granddaughter. (1) The arm needs to be clicked down into position, (2) you need to wind the car up the ramp (and the crank for that is tricky - if you let go just a little, it slides back to the bottom), then once the car slides down the ramp into the cradle you need to (3) release the arm for the catapult to launch down the second slide. Again - sounds complicated, right? But my granddaughter mastered it in no time! I was surprised and happy about that.

I was also very happy that she played with this over and over. She never seemed to get bored with it. The little car plays music and phrases as it goes along, and even when all the steps didn't go perfectly (ie: the car crashed), my granddaughter was amused. One quick note: some of the joints seem to come apart easily, and since toddlers are a little rough, we needed to keep an eye on this. Still, this will be a great toy that grows with our grandkids!
text_fidelity_b: VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park

text_fidelity_a:
Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Wrath of the Righteous Base Set We hold a monthly “Game Night” at our house and felt this was the perfect opportunity to introduce the Pathfinder Card game to our friends. Unfortunately, it took at least two hours to explain the rules of the game and our crowd is mostly people over 40, so keeping track of each character’s journey, remembering what powers they do or do not have, and explaining strategy was somewhat difficult, especially as everyone was a first time player. I think this game is best suited to a younger crowd (under 40) but it’s still fun for those who really stick with it.

A few of us played Dungeons & Dragons years ago, so this playing this felt very familiar. Every player is given the opportunity to "customize" their game play, in that they can choose to be a particular character. The characters are individually possessed of different powers, spells, weapons, and capabilities. You choose a specific character and a “scenerio” (a.k.a storyline) and draw cards that determine the path of your journey. Your objective is to maximize your advantage, using the cards and dice to advance or retreat. The objective, of course, is to win the game by overcoming monsters and capturing the bad guys for points. It’s like a video game in that they are different levels and you can move on to different stages. The game shifts scenes as you advance, so it feels like a continual maze. The game can technically go on forever as the company encourages you to buy “expansion sets” that give you additional cards and new adventures to go on.

Two people in our group are big science fiction and fantasy buffs, and they absolutely loved it. For the rest of us, it was challenging, and after playing this for two hours, a little tedious, since it requires so much thinking. This is not a game to be played when you’ve had a few cocktails! But for devoted game geeks, I can see this being a big hit.
text_fidelity_b: Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Wrath of the Righteous Base Set

NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version I've used a LOT of drones, from professional DJI models to the cheap pocket sized tiny drones. I love flying the little ones around the house and practicing zipping in between banisters and over bookcases, and I love flying my larger DJI Phantoms and Mavic outside for real shots of landscapes and aerial photography. I was hoping this would be a good in-between product.
It is not really.
It looks a lot like the Mavic Mini, but that immediately falls apart when you hold it and realize how cheap the construction is. That's ok, it costs about 1/3 of what I paid for my Mavic Mini. But I've held cheaper drones that felt better than this. The controls are very much like the cheaper smaller drones that have been around for years (including the flip feature, which is admittedly fun), and the quality of the camera has not improved since the first cheap one I tried 5-6 years ago. Find the most basic/free cell phone you can buy from a store shelf a few years ago and the camera quality will look better than this. That was ok back then, especially since I recall paying 40-60 dollars for those drones and the cheapest DJI was closer to 800! But now, I was expecting better. At this price tag and with 2022 tech, I was hoping it would be some sort of bridge-gap product.
The downside to being larger is that it sort of doesn't fit into either category... Unlike a more expensive drone with GPS and fine tuned motors, it does not handle itself well outdoors unless there is ZERO wind (nearly impossible, especially as you climb altitude), and it is too big to fly indoors without being in danger of hitting something and actually doing damage (unlike the smaller cheaper ones). I actually can't think of a situation that I'd like to use this with: I'd recommend a smaller camera drone to play with indoors and once you are approaching the triple digit dollar amount, I'd recommend even a used Mavic Mini for outdoor flying (much more stable with GPS, and a stabilized go-pro quality camera etc).
It does come with two batteries which is nice since they go quickly, and the carrying case is pretty nice too. I guess if you're in the market for a drone like this, it DOES work so it deserves at least 3 stars, but I'm slightly disappointed with what you get for the asking price.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version

The Settlers of Catan I have lost many a Sunday afternoon to Settlers. Do you know why I purchased Settlers? Because each of my friends has purchased our own set... we do not want to find ourselves at each others house and wanting to play but not have a board to set up. We have taken turns hosting and every time it has been fun.

It is a game of strategy, in my opinion a slightly more complicated/sophisticated version of Monopoly (although my friends vehemently disagree). Instead of building houses and hotels you build towns and cities, instead of collecting rent, you collect resources, and instead of chance cards you have victory cards... but somehow it seems more fun. There is an element of Chess- because you do have to build roads to tie your cities together, and to do that you have to have foresight and plan ahead.

This is a game of champions- and voted best Table Game by folks who vote on those things- be warned that once you start playing it may become addictive. Be prepared to be suckered into the sport for years to come.

I am reviewing this product in an effort to help other Amazon customers through relaying my experience with the product and providing any insight I garnered. text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Gaming Scattergories Board Game I have two teenagers who spend a lot of time in their rooms. We have the occasional game night once or twice a month for some quality family time. This game has become my 16 year old daughter's absolute favorite game. She has even started having her friends over for game night. You roll the dice and whatever letter comes up is the letter that each word that you write has to start with for that round. You are given a card that tells you what to write. For example, the card may say "a color" for number 1. The die was rolled and it landed on the letter G for that round. So you have to write down a color that starts with G on your list. Now if you and anyone else write the same G word, neither of you get a point. You are trying to come up with the most original and creative word that fits the letter and the subject. It's usually hard to come up with all twelve words in a round when the timer is set! We all enjoy this game!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Scattergories Board Game
